title: Blog Windows 11 Security Controls for Modern Devices
summary: Explore Windows 11 security controls that protect modern devices with Secure Boot, least privilege, encryption, passkeys, and cloud management.
body_markdown:
## **Key takeaways**


- Windows 11 security controls combine hardware-backed protection, least-privilege access, application control, encryption, and threat isolation to reduce endpoint risk.
- Secure Boot, TPM 2.0, and memory integrity help verify device integrity before and during startup.
- BitLocker and passkeys protect data and credentials if a device or password is compromised.
- Cloud-based management helps IT teams enforce security baselines, identify configuration drift, and maintain continuous compliance.


### In a[previous blog](https://www.insight.com/en_US/content-and-resources/blog/eight-device-security-best-practices-for-todays-workforce.html) , I spoke of a broader strategy behind device security and why it matters. Now we can get more specific calling out the actual controls, configurations, and protections that turn a Windows 11 device into a hardened, reliable endpoint.


When these pieces work together, the device becomes much harder to compromise and much easier to manage.


Think of this as the checklist your team should understand and feel comfortable applying. None of it is exotic. It is simply the modern baseline for a secure Windows device.


## How does secure boot protect Windows 11?


Everything begins with the boot chain. If the device cannot verify its own integrity at startup, nothing else truly matters.


[Windows 11](https://www.insight.com/en_US/shop/partner/microsoft/windows.html) uses Secure Boot to ensure only trusted firmware and bootloaders are allowed. This prevents tampering before the operating system loads. TPM 2.0 plays a major role here. It stores cryptographic measurements of the boot process so the device can confirm that nothing has been altered.


Memory integrity adds another layer by protecting the kernel from injection attacks. When this is enabled, the system uses virtualization to isolate critical processes. It’s a quiet control, but it blocks entire classes of exploits.


The goal is simple. When the device starts, you want to know it is starting clean.


## Enforce least privilege in Windows 11.


One of the most effective ways to protect a device is to remove local admin rights from everyday users. Most attacks rely on privilege escalation. If the user can’t install software, modify system settings, or run elevated commands, the attacker can’t either.


Windows 11 works well in a least privilege model. Standard users can do everything they need for normal work. When elevated access is required, you can use just-in-time admin tools or dedicated privileged access workstations.


This one change reduces risk dramatically. It also makes devices more predictable and easier to support.


## Block unauthorized apps in Windows 11.


Application control is one of the strongest defenses available. It stops malicious or unknown applications from running in the first place.


Smart App Control in Windows 11 uses AI to evaluate applications and decide whether they are trustworthy. It blocks unsigned or suspicious executables automatically. For more controlled environments, you can use allow listing policies through Intune or Windows Defender Application Control.


The idea is not to restrict users unnecessarily. It’s to prevent software that has no business running on the device from ever getting a foothold.


## Protect Windows 11 data with BitLocker.


Full disk encryption is essential. If a device is lost or stolen, you want to be confident that the data on it remains protected.


BitLocker provides strong encryption tied to the TPM. It unlocks seamlessly for authorized users and stays locked for everyone else. When combined with secure boot and passkeys, it creates a powerful chain of trust.


Encryption is one of the simplest controls to deploy, and it pays off every time a device leaves the building.


## Strengthen Windows 11 browser security.


Most attacks begin in the browser. Phishing, malicious downloads, drive-by exploits, and credential theft all start with a click.


Windows 11 includes several protections that make the browser safer. SmartScreen blocks known malicious sites and downloads. Application Guard isolates untrusted websites in a secure container. Enhanced phishing protection warns users when they enter credentials into suspicious pages.


These controls work quietly in the background, reducing the chances of a user being tricked or misled and making risky browsing far less dangerous.


## Why use passkeys in Windows 11?


Passwords are still the weakest link in most environments. Passkeys solve that problem.


A passkey is a cryptographic credential stored securely on the device. It can’t be phished, reused, or stolen from a server. When a user signs in with a passkey, they authenticate with something they have and something they are. Windows Hello makes this feel natural. The user simply looks at the camera or touches a sensor, and the device handles the rest.


### Passkeys are one of the most meaningful improvements you can make. They reduce credential theft dramatically and improve the user experience at the same time.


## Isolate threats with endpoint security.


Modern attacks often try to move laterally or exploit memory vulnerabilities. Device isolation features help stop that movement.


Windows 11 uses virtualization-based security to isolate sensitive processes. It also includes exploit protection settings that guard against common attack techniques. These controls don’t require constant tuning. They simply make the device more resilient.


When combined with EDR tools like Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, you get visibility into suspicious behavior and the ability to respond quickly.


## Maintain compliance with cloud management.


Modern device management platforms give you real-time insight into the health of your devices. Take Intune for example: It lets you enforce compliance policies, deploy baselines, and remediate issues automatically.


Continuous compliance means you do not wait for a problem to become visible. The system tells you when something drifts out of alignment, and you can fix it before it becomes a risk.


This is how you maintain a secure fleet without constant manual effort.
